text:
Olivia: Quick heads-up — just finished staging bring-up for lynx-embed-v2. Ran the standard recall/cluster suite and seeing a reproducible recall@10 drop vs lynx-embed-v1 baseline (~0.87 -> 0.82). Not huge but consistent across runs. Anyone digging into quantization/whitening differences?
Sam: ugh. is this on fp16 or int8 quantized?
Olivia: int8 per-tensor quant (our default fast path). FP16 baseline matches v1. int8 shows the drop.
Jia: can you paste the eval command + dataset? I'll kick off a few reproducibility runs.
Olivia: sure: `python eval_embeddings.py --model lynx-embed-v2 --quant int8 --dataset ms_marco --metric recall@10 --normalize cos`
Olivia: baseline v1 fp16: recall@10 = 0.872
Olivia: v2 int8: recall@10 = 0.819
Mike: that's ~5.3% absolute drop? or relative?
Olivia: 0.053 absolute (6% relative).
Jia: what about cosine vs dot? maybe scale mismatch after quantization.
Olivia: tried both. dot scaled by avg-norm didn't help much. cosine normalization gave the numbers above.
Sam: any shift in embedding norms distribution after quant? plot?
Olivia: quick summary: mean L2 pre-quant = 12.3, post-quant = 11.9, std widened slightly. clustering silhouette dropped from 0.41 -> 0.36.
Jia: hmm small norm shift could affect cosine if quant noise is anisotropic. Can you run per-channel int8 (if available) or dynamic-range clipping?
Olivia: will try per-channel next. also adding whitening transform in eval reduced the gap to ~0.02 but didn't fully close it.
Mike: what about k-NN index sensitivity? using HNSW params same? ef_search/ef_construction?
Olivia: yes identical HNSW params across runs. We reindexed both vectors from scratch.
Sam: can you throw up a quick PCA scatter for a few query clusters (v1 fp16 vs v2 int8)? even 2D t-SNE could show anisotropic noise.
Olivia: uploaded two PNGs to the staging artifact: link: https://staging-artifacts/redwood/lynx-v2-int8-pca.png and lynx-v1-fp16-pca.png
Jia: on it. also running `--quant perchannel` now. command: `python eval_embeddings.py --model lynx-embed-v2 --quant perchannel-int8 --dataset ms_marco`
Eval-bot: job 3476543210-1 queued on cluster-ml-5, estimated runtime 45m.
Sam: another dimension — did you change tokenization or pooling (mean vs cls)? small architectural tweaks can amplify quantization noise.
Olivia: pooling unchanged (mean pool). tokenizer unchanged. v2 has slightly deeper projection head (512->384) which might be more sensitive.
Jia: if per-channel closes gap, we should flag as a quantization profile requirement for v2 (per-channel only). if not, try cross-batch calibration with a larger calibration set (we used 10k samples earlier).
Mike: can we run recall broken down by query length / language? might be concentrated on short queries or non-en.
Olivia: breakdown posted: short queries (<6 tokens) drop = 0.07 absolute; long queries drop = 0.02. en drop ~0.04, other langs more noisy but smaller sample sizes.
Sam: sounds like short queries get noisier — maybe kv-cache / final norm amplification. try adding post-quant rescaling: `vec = vec * (orig_norm / quant_norm)` as a quick experiment.
Olivia: tried that hack — recovered ~0.015 of the gap but it's brittle. not a shipping fix.
Jia: per-channel run finished: recall@10 = 0.835. partial recovery but still ~0.037 below fp16.
Mike: per-channel helps — good signal that clipping/scale across channels was the culprit.
Sam: next steps: 1) try 16-bit hybrid (mantissa-8/exponent-8) if runtime ok 2) expand calibration set to 100k 3) evaluate whitening + per-channel together 4) add regression test to onboarding suite to fail if recall@10 drop > 0.02 5) document quant profile requirement for lynx-embed-v2.
Olivia: agree on gating. adding an eval ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/ML-7823 (PR incoming).
Jia: also add clustering metrics (silhouette, davies-bouldin) to the automated report so we catch anisotropic noise earlier.
Eval-bot: ran regression smoke: v1_fp16 vs v2_perchannel_int8 summary: recall@10 delta = -0.037, silhouette delta = -0.03.
Mike: thanks — if per-channel is required, we should weigh cost impact (memory/runtime). ops: how much slower?
Olivia: per-channel int8 regression on staging: +5% latency at p95 and +8% GPU memory. not ideal but maybe acceptable for Dedicated tier.
Sam: ok let's draft a recommendation: - Default fast path remains fp16 for hosted low-tier - For v2, require per-channel int8 for Dedicated customers or provide a quant-profile flag that forces fp16 for small query workloads - Add regression gate at 0.02 absolute recall@10 loss blocker.
Olivia: I'll open the PR with perf numbers and add the regression gate. tagging infra/ops to weigh cost tradeoff. :eyes:
Jia: I'll run expanded calibration and a final HNSW sensitivity sweep overnight.
Mike: thanks team. if anyone else has quick ideas for mitigation (e.g., layernorm clipping, post-quant norm correction), drop them here. :thumbsup:
